mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of industrial contraction (INDPRO < 100), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals further weakening in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate profit expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when INDPRO < 100 and INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL 1-mo change) exceeding 3.0% signals an accelerating inflation trend that may lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when CPIAUCSL 1-mo change exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods of PAYEMS growth, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL 1-mo change) signals a 'higher for longer' monetary policy stance, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL 1-mo change rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when UNRATE falls below 3.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
